script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Good morning! I'm Dr. Martinez. I see we have both Emma and little Jake here for their well-child visits today.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Yes, thank you for fitting them both in. Emma just turned 5 last month and Jake is 2 and a half now.

script.speaker: child
script.text: I'm five! I can count to one hundred!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Wow, that's impressive Emma! Let's start with you since you're the big sister. How has she been doing overall?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She's been pretty good. I'm a little worried about her eating though - she's gotten very picky lately. And she's been complaining about her tummy hurting sometimes.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's very common at this age. When does the tummy pain usually happen?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Usually in the mornings before preschool, but then she seems fine once she gets there. I wonder if it's just nerves?

script.speaker: child
script.text: My tummy hurts when I don't want to go to school.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That sounds like it could be some anxiety about school transitions. Very normal. Let me check Emma's growth first.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: She's 41 inches tall and weighs 38 pounds - right on track for her age. Any concerns about her development or behavior?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: She's doing well in preschool. Reading some words already. But she still has accidents sometimes, especially when she's really focused on playing.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's completely normal at 5. Emma, can you hop on one foot for me?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Like this? One, two, three, four!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Perfect! Now let me listen to your heart. Can you take big breaths like a dragon?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Roooooaaaaar! Am I healthy?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Very healthy! Now let's check on Jake. How's he been doing?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: He's been good but he's had some trouble sleeping through the night lately. And I'm worried he's not talking as much as Emma did at this age.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: What kind of words is he using? Can he put two words together?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: He says 'mama,' 'dada,' 'more,' 'no' - that's his favorite. He can say 'want cookie' or 'go car' but not much more.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That sounds appropriate for 2 and a half. Boys often develop language a bit later than girls. Let me examine him.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Jake is 34 inches and 28 pounds - great growth. His ears look clear, throat looks good. Any medications for either child?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Emma takes those Flintstones vitamins daily, and Jake gets children's Tylenol when he's teething or has a fever.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: The vitamins are fine to continue. For the Tylenol, you can give Jake up to 240 milligrams every 4 hours as needed for pain or fever.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Okay, I usually just follow what's on the box. Is that the right amount for his weight?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Yes, that dose should work well for him. Any allergies to medications for either child?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: No known allergies. Emma did get a rash from some bubble bath once, but nothing with medicines.

script.speaker: child
script.text: The bubbles made me itchy!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: We'll note that. Now, are both children up to date on their vaccines?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: I think so. Emma got some shots at her 4-year visit, and Jake had his 2-year shots a few months ago.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Let me check their records. Emma needs her pre-K boosters today - DTaP, IPV, MMR, and Varicella. Jake looks current.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Oh no, Emma hates shots. Will she need all of those?

script.speaker: child
script.text: I don't want shots! They hurt!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: I know sweetheart, but these vaccines keep you healthy and protect your friends too. We can use a numbing cream to help.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: What about Jake's sleep issues? He's been waking up 2-3 times a night for the past month.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Is he having nightmares, or just waking up? Any changes in his routine lately?

script.speaker: parent
script.text: No nightmares that I know of. He just wakes up crying. We did move him to a toddler bed last month.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: That's likely the culprit. Big transitions can disrupt sleep. Try a consistent bedtime routine and maybe a comfort object.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: He has his stuffed elephant. Should I let him cry it out or go to him?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: You can try briefly comforting him without picking him up, then gradually reduce your response time. It may take a few weeks.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Okay. And about Emma's eating - she basically only wants mac and cheese and chicken nuggets now.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Very typical for her age. Keep offering variety alongside her preferred foods. Don't turn meals into battles.

script.speaker: child
script.text: I like mac and cheese! It's yellow!

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Yellow is a great color! Maybe we can find other yellow foods you might like too.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Any other concerns I should watch for at these ages?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: For Emma, continue working on independence and emotional regulation. For Jake, watch for more language development over the next six months.

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Let's get Emma's vaccines done, and I'll see both of them again in a year unless you have concerns before then.

script.speaker: parent
script.text: Thank you. This has been really helpful. Emma, you ready to be brave?

script.speaker: child
script.text: Will I get a sticker after?

script.speaker: doctor
script.text: Of course! You can pick two stickers since you're being so brave.
